messages.author: 72e6c75f8e833003
messages.subject: freqC freqT
parts:
Hi I just had a simple question regarding the set up of the test files,
I assume coverage = total reads mapped in the cytosine, and freqC = number of methylated cytosines, freqT = unmethylated cytosines mapped?
Please correct me if I am wrong.

Thanks.
-------
Jawon Song, Ph.D.,
Research Engineering/Scientist Associate
Life Sciences Computing Group
Texas Advanced Computing Center
Austin, TX

messages.author: ab8277113f65c05e
messages.subject: Re: freqC freqT
parts:
Generally speaking Yes. However, some alignment pipelines will output coverage as (number of Cs + number of Ts). Sometimes, you will not have only C or T  on a position due to alignment errors, read quality issues or SNPs. I think it is best to equalise coverage to (number of Cs + number of Ts) not to the total reads mapped to that position.


Best,
Altuna
